headline: Moderate outlook for long outages in Travis County
summary: Homes in Travis County lose power for 12 hours or more about once every 11 years. That comes from 8 years of records since 2018. The largest outage here began on February 14, 2021. At its peak, 43% of homes in the county were dark. For a home with electric heat, one Core lasts about 18 hours in August and about 35 hours in March. We suggest two Cores. That would have covered 77% of past long outage hours. Base confirms sizing at install.
